instruction: Design the home/hub screen (a single page) for a "Spirit Summoning" game. Include: the game title, an atmospheric hero area, a currency (gold) indicator, and the main menu as cards or buttons (Summon / Roster / Battle / Grind). Put strong emphasis on the visual design: a beautiful, mystical game menu with a distinct mood, clear hierarchy, and crafted cards — careful color, typography and finish. Make this screen look genuinely polished.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The four-rite menu (Summon / Roster / Battle / Grind) is the heart of a hub, yet it is pushed below the fold and visually truncated to two card-tops, so only Summon and Roster are legible and the required menu is not substantively delivered in-frame. Worse, the hero duplicates Summon and Roster as buttons, splitting navigation across two zones and blurring which is the real menu. Trade-off: a tall, atmospheric hero (good mood) is winning the screen at the expense of the routing function a hub exists to perform. Clarity & Hierarchy: Three navigation entry points compete (gold SUMMON, ghost VIEW ROSTER, and the card row), so the eye has no single next step. The 120px hero wordmark repeats the top-left logo, spending the strongest type moment on brand instead of action. The Power/Spirits/Win-Streak row is low-contrast and floats weakly under the buttons, and the right-aligned 'Choose a rite…' line under THE SANCTUM is tiny and disconnected from its heading. Visual System & Craft: The indigo + gold + teal palette and serif-display/sans-body pairing are coherent and on-mood (a genuine strength), but vertical rhythm is broken — a large empty band sits mid-left between hero and COMMAND while the bottom is overcrowded and clipped. The '+100' badge uses a green that breaks the gold/teal system, the avatar is a generic placeholder glyph, the sigil's left glow crowds the title's right edge, and the orb's teal diamond reads flatter than the surrounding craft. Expressiveness: The astrolabe sigil and the 'THE VEIL IS THINNING' eyebrow are genuinely authored, memorable moments, but distinctiveness is concentrated in one ornament; the menu cards that should carry per-rite identity are too hidden to read, and the two visible ones only hint at color-coding (gold vs teal) without completing the system — so the hub's voice lives in the hero, not in the navigation the player actually uses.
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (all self-contained: CSS gradients + inline SVG only, no external assets). P1 — Rebalance so the menu is the clear primary nav and fully visible: reduce the sigil diameter ~20–25%, tighten the hero-to-COMMAND gap, and lift the four cards (Summon / Roster / Battle / Grind) into or immediately at the first viewport so none are clipped; make the equal-height, corner-bracketed cards the visual anchor of the lower half. P2 — Kill the CTA duplication: hero keeps exactly one primary CTA, SUMMON (the core-loop hook); remove VIEW ROSTER from the hero so Roster lives only in the menu, leaving hero = atmosphere + one action and the cards = the full menu (Summon intentionally mirrored as the hero CTA). P3 — Give each rite card its own identity so the nav is crafted and scannable: Summon = gold (500g / pull), Roster = teal (128 bound), Battle = ember/crimson (e.g. Win streak 6), Grind = verdant/bone (e.g. Daily rites); color each card's icon, accent line, and badge to its hue, turning four boxes into a color-coded menu and moving expressiveness into the navigation. P4 — Hierarchy & craft fixes: shrink the top-left logo to mark + small wordmark so the big hero title is the single title moment; restyle the stats as one thin, hairline-divided, higher-contrast strip aligned to the sigil baseline; move the 'Choose a rite…' helper to a left-aligned subtitle directly under THE SANCTUM at readable size; recolor the '+100' badge to a palette-consistent gold/teal gain tone; replace the placeholder avatar with a sigil-framed emblem; add left margin between the title's right edge and the sigil glow, and give the orb's teal diamond a subtle inner gradient to match the craft level. P5 — Polish: add hover/active states on cards and buttons (lift + accent glow), unify corner radii, and seat the sigil with a faint ground glow/vignette so the scene feels grounded rather than floating.
